condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

description.narrative: 1.1 A territorial spatial development plan in Upper Egypt is finalized, approved and in use by relevant local authorities. 1.2 A territorial spatial development plan in Delta is finalized, approved and in use by relevant local authorities. 1.3 A territorial spatial development plan in a border/coastal zone is finalized, approved and in use by relevant local authorities. 1.4 All prepared territorial plans consider an overall enhancement of gender sensitive service provision (education, health, employment), ensuring equal access for women and men. 2.1 A performance- based assessment plans for two cities in Upper Egypt are prepared and in use. 2.2 A performance- based assessment plans for two cities in Delta are prepared and in use. 2.3 A performance- based assessment plans for two cities in a border/coastal zone are prepared and in use. 2.4 All prepared performance based assessment consider the assessment of gender sensitive service provision (education, health, employment), ensuring equal access for women and men. 3.1 A legal/institutional framework and an interurban management mechanism published and in-use. 3.2 A coordination/participation framework between authorities and other stakeholders is published, approved and circulated. 3.3 A territorial spatial development guidelines document is published and in use by relevant authorities. 4.1 A territorial land information system (LIS) linked to GOPP’s GIS enterprise functional. 4.2 Capacity building programs and on-the-job training in planning, management and IT/GIS produced. All programs target a balanced participation of men and women 4.3 A project management framework adopted.

- A territorial development plan and implementation mechanisms of a pilot case in Upper Egypt and Delta are developed - Outline processes, methods and tools for the performance-based city development planning - Performance-based assessment of two cities (existing and new) in Upper Egypt are developed - A territorial land information system (LIS) linked to GOPP’s GIS enterprise is functional

- The territorial spatial development plan in Upper Egypt is in progress - Workgroup formulated for the territorial spatial development plan in Delta - The performance-based assessment plans for two cities in Upper Egypt are in progress. - First report defining approaches, indicators and criteria prepared to develop a territorial spatial development guidelines document - GIS/LIS data needs assessed for the territorial land information system (LIS) linked to GOPP’s GIS enterprise - 2 capacity building programs took place on urban institutional governance and smart cities, and on management of urbanism and development withing urban territories/agglomerations, with a total number of 33 attendess (40% women and 60% men)

-Investigate general gaps, needs and opportunities in existing and new settlements in Egypt (Define priorities for development) -Prepare a territorial development plan and implementation mechanisms of a pilot case study in Upper Egypt -Prepare a territorial development plan and implementation mechanisms of a pilot case study in Delta -Prepare a performance-based assessment of two cities (existing and new) in Upper Egypt -A Legal/institutional framework and an interurban management mechanism published and in-use -Prepare and implement capacity building programs and on-the-job training in planning, management and IT/GIS

-Two additional pilot projects were selected in the delta region: the Sadat agglomeration which include the new Sadat city as well as several cities and rural units in both Beheira and Menoufia governorates, and in the coastal region: Damietta agglomeration which include Damietta city, New Damietta city as well as selected urban and rural units surrounding both cities. The three selected pilots represent different planning challenges that are investigated differently in terms of planning approach.
-6 coordination meetings with the group of experts were held in GOPP to follow up with the preparation of the sectoral working papers. In parallel, the final report of the territorial planning of the Beni Suef agglomeration was prepared. The final report includes the following: 1. The final delineation of the pilot case study boundary. 2. An analysis of the urban, socio-economic and environmental challenges in the agglomeration 3. An analysis of the interrelationships between the different urban components of the agglomeration, including the economic functions and networks. 4. The definition of the gaps in services, housing, economic activities between the new city and the existing city. 5. Formulation of a set of policies, directives and recommendations to improve the synergies between the two cities. 6. Formulation of a set of performance indicators that represent each sector. 7. Setting up an implementation mechanisms to enable the effective implementation of the recommended policies and directives. A visit to the Governorate was carried out in August 2022. During this visit the Final Tretorial plan was presented by the workgroup to the Governor. The meetings with the Governor and local stakeholders highlighted the main development issues, the propsed instituional framework to achieve a territorial synergy between the new city and other existing settlements was discussed.
-A site visit was carried out to New Sadat city. The visit includes a meeting with the Head of the city authority and its executive board to establish a coordination platform and to ensure the participation of the stakeholders in the work progress. Another meeting was held with Sadat’s investors association to ensure their continuous contribution to the project’s outputs. ? The delineation of a spatial boundary for the agglomeration was a challenging task. This is due to the complexity of relationships and roles of the different surrounding settlements in both Beheira and Menoufia governorates. A set of criteria was discussed with the project’s consultants. The GIS expert translated those criteria into maps using different geospatial analysis techniques. ? To support the definition of the boundary and to better understand the dynamics of mobility between the different urban nodes and centers in the agglomeration, a questionnaire was designed and disseminated in Sadat city and its industrial zone. The sample size was 1000 persons. The project team analyzed the responses and the preliminary results are presented to the workgroup. ? Performance measurement indicators are prepared and collected. ? Sectoral studies are prepared and revised. ? The final report of the agglomeration development is prepared. It includes chapters on the vision formulation, goals and strategies, development scenarios, and the final strategic development plan for the agglomeration.
-The final documentation of the Beni Suef pilot project was developed and includes a set of performance-based indicators that assists in the assessment and monitoring of implementation progress.
-Two reports on the proposed model for institutional organization and management of the agglomeration were prepared
-The following capacity building programs were accomplished with 66% of trainees were females: 1. Applications of GIS in land management (land information systems) – Part One: this course was prepared in collaboration with Housing and Building National Research Center (HRBC) and ESRI (from 6/3/2022 – to 10/3/2022). This course aimed at improving the basic participants skills in using land information systems and their geospatial applications. 2. Applications of GIS in land management (land information systems) – Part Two: this course was also prepared in collaboration with Housing and Building National Research Center (HRBC) and ESRI (from 20/3/2022 – to 24/3/2022). This course aimed at providing the participants with more advanced hands-on the vector and raster based applications to solve spatial problems using modelling techniques. 3. Providing the technical support to incorporate SDGs in urban projects, and to define performance-based indicators in light of the COVID pandemics: this three days training program was prepared in collaboration with HRBC. It targeted the high level management staff of GOPP during the period from 15-17 May 2022. 4. The project also carried out an agreement with the Faculty of regional and urban planning, Cairo University. This agreement provided an opportunity for 25 GOPP staff to pursue their studies through the technical diploma ‘ the management and governance of urban areas’ 5. Two additional capacity building programs were executed in October 2022 in the fields of result-based project management and in urban governance.
